identity.description: Bagged decision-tree ensemble: each tree is fit on a bootstrap resample with a random feature subset per split, and predictions are averaged. Variance reduction by averaging — not additive error correction like boosting — makes it a robust, low-tuning tabular baseline that rarely embarrasses itself.

emits.note: classification; averaged leaf class fractions across trees — well-ranked but compressed toward the center (rarely near 0/1), so calibration sharpens the extremes
regression mode; per-tree leaf means averaged
via SHAP (TreeExplainer), not native per-row; impurity and permutation importances are native but global-only

n_estimators.note: more trees never hurt accuracy (averaging converges), only compute — unlike boosting there is no overfit-by-iteration axis

max_features.note: the decorrelation knob — the smaller the per-split feature subset, the less correlated the trees and the more averaging buys

invariances.why: every split is a threshold comparison on one feature; any monotone rescale yields identical trees in every ensemble member
the best-split search depends only on feature ORDER, so log/rank/box-cox of an input cannot change any tree in the forest

sklearn >=1.4 forests route missing values down the lower-impurity child (learned direction) for dense numeric input; a driver pinned below 1.4 must impute — version-gated, hence empirical not mechanism
sklearn trees require numeric input; categoricals must be pre-encoded (no native categorical splitter in this library, unlike LightGBM)
a non-parametric ensemble of partitions makes no assumption about the marginal or error distribution
bootstrap averaging keeps variance in check even at a few hundred rows where boosting overfits; scales to large n with n_jobs parallelism
predictions are averages of piecewise-constant leaves; outside the training range every tree clamps to its boundary leaf

featureStats.why: each split partitions the bootstrap sample; low n/p leaves too few rows per leaf for the per-split feature lottery to find signal — a gate toward regularized linear
bootstrap resampling reproduces the imbalance inside every tree, so minority leaves are rare; severe skew shifts the honest metric to PR-AUC/lift and suggests class_weight='balanced'
high missingness is where learned NaN routing (sklearn >=1.4) is an advantage worth citing over impute-then-linear, and where imputation would erase the missingness signal

modelMetrics.why: bagging leaves ~37% of rows out of each tree, giving a free unbiased generalization estimate; OOB diverging from CV flags leakage or non-iid rows — a lens boosting cannot offer
if a linear model ties the forest, the ensemble's opacity and compute are not earning their keep — a commit-linear signal
one feature owning most impurity importance is the leakage-dominance signature the promotion gate blocks

edgeCases.behavior: bootstrap resamples nearly coincide; trees correlate and the variance-reduction mechanism has nothing to average away
impurity importance biases toward the wide block; per-split feature subsets are flooded by near-empty dummies
every tree splits it first; forest degenerates to one tree's decision

driver.threadSafety: n_jobs-parallel fit and predict; fitted estimator is read-only thread-safe

canBeSeeds.note: RF probabilities are center-compressed by averaging — the textbook calibration customer

placementClaims.why: learned NaN routing (driver floor sklearn>=1.4) makes upstream imputation unnecessary and sometimes harmful — it erases the missingness signal
monotone-transform-invariant: log/Yeo-Johnson cannot change any tree's split structure
scale-insensitive by mechanism; standardization is wasted compute
sklearn trees need categoricals encoded to numeric before fit
